nodes.summary: For a clause kind $c$ of a cell with $g$ symbol codes and an index $l$, the label the generator moves to once literals $l, l+1, \dots$ of $c$ have been emitted (literals are emitted from the last one down to the first): if $l = 0$, the final stage of clause $c$, which emits the leading run of empty slots; otherwise the routine for literal $l - 1$ of $c$, or the halting label when $l - 1 \ge g$.
nodes.title: Label after a literal routine of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For $g, B \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the $g$ positive literals on the variables $v_B, v_{B+1}, \dots, v_{B+g-1}$, in this order, each given as the pair of its variable index and the sign true; these are the literals of the clause $v_B \lor \dots \lor v_{B+g-1}$.
nodes.title: At-least-one literals of a cell

nodes.summary: For $B, x, y \in \mathbb{N}$, the two-element list of the negative literals on the variables $v_{B+x}$ and $v_{B+y}$, in this order, each given as the pair of its variable index and the sign false; these are the literals of the clause $\neg v_{B+x} \lor \neg v_{B+y}$. It is used for pairs $x < y$.
nodes.title: At-most-one literals for a pair

nodes.summary: For a layout $L$ with $g$ symbol codes, natural numbers $T, H$, a time step $t$ and a stack $k$, the concatenation over $j = 0, \dots, H - 1$ of the bit encodings of the one-hot clauses of the cell whose base is the cell variable of $L$ for stack $k$, depth $j$, symbol code $0$ at time $t$, written densely over the $V$ variables of $L$ for $T$ and $H$.
nodes.title: Encoded one-hot clauses of one stack at one time step

nodes.summary: For a layout $L$ with $K$ stacks, natural numbers $T, H$ and a time step $t$, the concatenation over the stacks $k = 0, \dots, K - 1$ of the encoded one-hot clauses of stack $k$ at time step $t$ (for $T$ and $H$).
nodes.title: Encoded one-hot clauses of one time step

nodes.summary: For $V, B \in \mathbb{N}$, a clause kind $c$ and an index $l$, the number $B + o_l$ if $l$ is less than the number of literals of $c$, where $o_l$ is the offset of literal $l$ of $c$ from the cell base, and $V$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Boundary before a literal of a cell clause

nodes.summary: For $g, H, V \in \mathbb{N}$, the number $2V + 2 + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (1 + g^2)\, b + V + 1$, where $b$ is the step bound for one clause for $g$ and $V$. It bounds the steps of one iteration of the one-hot generator's loop over cell depths.
nodes.title: Step bound for one cell

nodes.summary: For $g, V, B \in \mathbb{N}$, the CNF formula whose first clause is the at-least-one clause $v_B \lor \dots \lor v_{B+g-1}$ and whose remaining clauses are the at-most-one clauses $\neg v_{B+x} \lor \neg v_{B+y}$ for $x < y < g$, ordered by $y$ and then by $x$. Each clause is written densely over the $V$ variables $v_0, \dots, v_{V-1}$; literals on variables of index at least $V$ are dropped.
nodes.title: One-hot clauses of a cell

nodes.title: Generator run for one cell

nodes.summary: The finite type of the nineteen unit counters of the one-hot clause generator: Tn, Ti, Kc, Kd, Hs, Hi, Gc, HG, Wc, Vc, TW, KB, CB, P, Q, tmp, md, c1 and c2.
nodes.title: Counters of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For a natural number $g$, a clause kind of a cell with $g$ symbol codes is either the at-least-one kind, or the at-most-one kind of a pair $(x, y)$ of symbol codes $x, y < g$ (not necessarily ordered).
nodes.title: Clause kinds of a one-hot cell

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $g$ and $V$, the step budget for one clause is $V(3V + 6) + g(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$, where $6V + 9$ is the per-literal cost apart from the gap loop.
nodes.title: Step budget for one one-hot clause

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a layout with $g$ symbol codes, let $c$ be a well-formed clause kind of a cell (the pair of an at-most-one kind is increasing), and let $B$ and $V$ be natural numbers with $B + g \le V$. nodes.title: One clause of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For a cell base $B$ and a clause kind $c$ of a cell with $g$ symbol codes, the literals of $c$ form a list of pairs (variable, sign): for the at-least-one kind, the pairs $(B + x, \mathrm{true})$ for $x = 0, \dots, g - 1$ in increasing order; for the at-most-one kind of the pair $(x, y)$, the two pairs $(B + x, \mathrm{false})$ and $(B + y, \mathrm{false})$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $g$, the labels are: a precomputation label for each precomputation stage; for the time loop, a head, a rest label, a multiplication label for each multiplication stage, and an end label; for the stack loop, a head, a rest label, an emission label, two copy labels, a multiplication label for each multiplication stage, and an end label; for the depth loop, a head, a rest label, two copy labels,…
nodes.title: Control labels of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $T$ and $H$, the initial counter values are $T$ on the counter $\mathrm{Tn}$, $H$ on the counter $\mathrm{Hs}$, and $0$ on every other counter.
nodes.title: Initial counters of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $g$, $K$, $H$ and $V$, let $c = V(3V + 6) + g(6V + 9) + 3V + 4$ be the step budget for one clause and $C = 2V + 2 + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (1 + g^2)c + V + 1$ the step budget for one cell. The budget is $1 + (2V + 2) + (K(2Hg + 3) + K + 2) + (H(C + 1) + H + 2) + V + 1$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $V$, the cost of emitting one literal, apart from the gap loop, is $6V + 9$.
nodes.title: Per-literal step cost of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For a clause kind $c$ of a cell with $g$ symbol codes and a natural number $l$, the entry label of literal $l$ of $c$ is the first-stage label of the routine emitting literal $l$ of $c$ if $l < g$, and the halting label otherwise.

nodes.summary: The stages of the routine of the one-hot generator that emits one literal are: two copy stages, the offset stage, the decrement stage, the comparison stage, for each ordering $o$ (less, equal, greater) two restore stages $r(o)$ and $r_B(o)$, the gap stage, the failure stage, the slot stage and the drain stage.

nodes.summary: The offset from the cell base of literal $l$ of a clause kind is $l$ for the at-least-one clause, and for the at-most-one clause $\mathrm{amo}(x, y)$ it is $x$ when $l = 0$ and $y$ otherwise.

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k \ge 1$ and $y \ge 1$, the explicit time bound of the one-hot generator for the layout whose label block size, number of stacks, number of symbol codes and window depth all equal $k$, with $T = H = y$, is at most $668\, k^7 y^6$.
nodes.title: Time bound of the one-hot generator on a uniform layout

nodes.summary: For a layout $L$ and natural numbers $T$ and $H$, the explicit time bound of the one-hot generator is $p + (T + 1)(b + 1) + (T + 1) + 2$, where $p$ is the cost of its precomputation and $b$ the cost of one iteration of its time loop, both for $L$, $T$ and $H$.
nodes.title: Explicit time bound of the one-hot generator

nodes.summary: For a layout $L$ with label block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, the constant of the one-hot generator's time bound is $668\,(A + K + g + 1)^7$; it does not depend on the window depth of $L$.

For natural numbers $T$ and $H$, its value at $X = T + H$ is $c\,(T + H + 1)^6$, the bound on the number of steps of the one-hot generator started on $T$ and $H$.

nodes.summary: The one-hot generator for a layout, bundled as a Mathlib multi-stack Turing machine with finitely many stacks, labels and internal states: its stacks are the output bit stack and one unary counter for each counter of the generator, its input stack is the time counter and its output stack is the output stack, it starts at its first precomputation label with internal state false, and it runs the generator's program.
nodes.title: The one-hot generator as a finite multi-stack machine

nodes.summary: Fix a number $g$ of symbol codes. For natural numbers $x$ and $y$ with $x < y < g$, the generator label at which the emission of the at-most-one clause for the pair $(x, y)$ of the current cell begins; for any other pair it is the halting label, a case the generator never uses.

nodes.summary: For a layout with label/state block size $A$, $K$ stacks and $g$ symbol codes, bounds $T$ and $H$, and row width $W = A + KHg$, the number of steps allotted to the generator's precomputation is $4 + (H(2g + 3) + H + 2) + (K(2Hg + 3) + K + 2) + ((T + 1)(2W + 3) + (T + 1) + 2)$.

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be the number of symbol codes of the one-hot generator. For a natural number $y$, this is the label of the generator at which the at-least-one clause starts when $y \le 1$; when $2 \le y \le g$, the label starting the at-most-one clause for the pair $(y - 2, y - 1)$; and when $y \ge 2$ and $y > g$, the final label $\mathrm{done}$.

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
